sam: quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture to chase a kernel-selection flip that shows up ~10s after warmup. suspicion: KV-cache ramp + batch size change triggers a different cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel.
jia: can you paste the exact nsys command you used? want to try a repro locally.
sam: sure, here's the minimal command i used:
```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=auto --duration=20s -o tmp/flip_run
```
sam: i also wrapped the critical sections in NVTX markers around the batching/kvcache code.
esther: 20s might be too short if warmup plus one offending request happens late — increase duration to 60s and do a longwarmup pass first :eyes:
sam: good point. adding warmup and a slightly different capture flag i tried:
```bash
# warmup (50 iters)
python -m perf_runner --seq-dist=short --iters=50
# then capture
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=60s --capture-range=process:$(pidof server) -o tmp/flip_long
```
tim: also try toggling sampling vs. full range — sampling hides short-lived kernel switches. i usually do two runs: sampling-mode for overview and full-trace for kernel timeline. e.g.
- sampling: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=30s` (quick hotspot scan)
- full: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=120s --capture-range=pid:1234`
jia: to zero in on kv-cache handoff, add NVTX spans before/after cache refill and annotate sequence length. that makes it trivial to align timeline to batch boundary in the GUI.
sam: observed timeline: before flip, small kernels from kernel_A (fp16 optimized). after refresh, we see larger kernel_B (fp32 fallback). suspect quantized codepath misses for certain sequence lengths.
esther: when you see a flip, check the kernel launch params (sm, blocks, shared mem) in the nsys kernel table — it usually hints at either a different algorithm or a cudnn heuristic decision.
tim: another cheap trick: enable osrt markers in nsys and show OSRT thread lanes — you can see GPU submission gaps correlated with KV eviction spikes.
sam: attached a quick snippet of the nvtx annotations i used (logged via our util):
```python
with nvtx.annotate("batch_start", color="0x00ff00"):
    model.run_batch(inputs)
with nvtx.annotate("kvcache_refresh", color="0xff0000"):
    kvcache.refill(prefixes)
```
jia: if you can upload the qdrep and qureps we can diff two captures and inspect kernel timeline deltas.
sam: uploaded -> https://storage.internal/tmp/flip_long.qdrep (nsys-bot posted artifact link)
nsys-bot: artifact uploaded: /tmp/flip_long.qdrep — use `nsys-ui` or `nsys stats` to inspect.
esther: when diffing, filter kernels by name and launch dims; look for sudden jumps in register usage or dynamic shared mem — cudnn sometimes picks a different algo when those cross thresholds.
tim: also check for controller-side batching heuristic logs — sometimes the client-side batching pushes a one-off super-long sequence that breaks the steady-state distribution.
sam: confirmed: one request with seq_len=2048 caused a cache refill and changed the sequence length distribution, after which kernel_B shows up.
ja: for a cheap regression guard, add a small unit test that asserts no kernel-algo-change for our common seq length percentile (p95) under x warmup iterations.
esther: also consider a lightweight capture with `--sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx` but short duration to make a small qdrep that still contains kernel metadata.
sam: thanks all — will run the 2-mode captures (sampling + full) and post the diffs. if anyone wants to pair on the qdrep diff later ping me. :thumbsup:
